unit_attributes.statement: For library lending, an access record (AR) means the dated entry of a visitor's permission to borrow.
An access record is not an annual report.
For finance reporting, an annual report (AR) means the signed yearly account of spending.
In the finance rules following this statement, AR always means annual report.
You must sign and date the annual report (AR) before submitting it.
Signing and dating are both required.
Visitors do not need an access record for a public tour.
Librarians do not need an access record to enter the archive.
The public tour exemption for visitors and the archive entry exemption for librarians are separate exemptions for different activities.
If an access record is lost and remains unreported for more than a month, staff must request a replacement.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If an access record is lost and remains unreported for more than a month

unit_attributes.statement: If an access record is lost and remains unreported for more than a month, and if travel is imminent, a temporary pass may be issued.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If an access record is lost and remains unreported for more than a month, and if travel is imminent

unit_attributes.statement: Finance reviewers should check the annual report (AR) for missing pages.
Missing pages may indicate an incomplete submission.
An annual report must not be altered without the director's approval.
The director approves alterations; this sentence does not identify who would perform an alteration.
Staff must file the access record.
Staff must retain the access record for two years.
